findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Route the un-verified hard-size-cap capability for /var/tmp and overlay2 writable container layers on XFS to a SPIKE (or explicitly downgrade the AC wording to distinguish a true size ceiling from age/count reaping) before committing child stories to 'enforced cap' language.
evidence: Plan: '/var/tmp (tmpfiles cleanup plus a real size/quota mechanism where required)'
Plan: 'writable container layers (runtime storage quota where supportable, or bounded periodic reaping of exited containers)'
S0 ADR draft consequences: '/var/tmp may need a separate quota-backed path or size-enforcing service because tmpfiles alone primarily supplies age cleanup on XFS'
AC asserts an unconditional 'enforced cap' for every named accumulator, but two accumulators have UNVERIFIED hard-size enforcement on XFS — an asserted-but-unverified capability the AC depends on
T3 overlay: 'a critical capability gap should route to a SPIKE before committing the full plan'
findings.finding: The plan asserts a HARD SIZE cap for every named root accumulator (AC: 'Each named root accumulator has an enforced cap'), but for /var/tmp and the overlay2 writable container layer it simultaneously concedes the enabling capability may not exist ('a real size/quota mechanism where required', 'runtime storage quota where supportable, or bounded periodic reaping'), and the S0 ADR consequences state 'tmpfiles alone primarily supplies age cleanup on XFS'. This is a named capability gap between an age-cleanup/reaping mechanism and a true size ceiling on XFS, yet it is not routed to a SPIKE before committing the full cap-everything plan.
findings.location: Design item 1 (Option A) and AC line 'Each named root accumulator has an enforced cap'; S0 ADR consequences
scenarios: A child story attempts to enforce a hard size cap on /var/tmp on XFS and discovers tmpfiles only ages files out, leaving the accumulator effectively uncapped while the AC is marked satisfied
A child story finds Docker/overlay2 offers no per-writable-layer size quota on the host storage driver and silently falls back to periodic reaping, which bounds count/age but not peak size
findings.suggested_fix: Add a spike child story that probes, on the target XFS host, whether a hard size ceiling is achievable for /var/tmp (e.g., XFS project quota or a dedicated mounted filesystem) and for the overlay2 writable layer (storage driver quota support), and gate the Option-A implementation stories on its finding; reword the AC to require either an enforced size cap or, where the spike shows it is unsupportable, a named bounded-reaping fallback with its own alarm.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Assign a child (or add an epic-level regression AC/test) that asserts the existing root/data disk alarms remain present and the cyclopean treat_missing_data=breaching fix is not regressed.
evidence: Parent AC line: '- [ ] Existing root/data disk alarms remain present; the cyclopean missing-data fix is not regressed.'

Roster absence check: S0's ACs are ADR-only; S1's ACs add a NEW scratch alarm; S2's ACs 'declares dedicated CloudWatch alarms' (new) and only references the existing root alarm text as grounding, not as a preservation obligation; S3/S4/S5 each add a NEW dedicated alarm and say nothing about the pre-existing root alarm (monitoring_autodeploy.tf:207-239) or data alarm (monitoring.tf:217-244).
No child AC mentions treat_missing_data / notBreaching->breaching or otherwise guards the cyclopean missing-data fix from regression.
Parent Context states Defect 2's treat_missing_data fix 'stays on that bug' but the parent still asserts AC4 as an epic acceptance criterion, so it must be delivered by a child or epic-level check.
findings.finding: Parent AC4 ('Existing root/data disk alarms remain present; the cyclopean missing-data fix is not regressed') is uncovered by the union of children's acceptance criteria.
findings.location: children collectively (no owner); nearest is child 9183-aaae-667d-45e6 (S2)
scenarios: A child editing monitoring_autodeploy.tf to add per-generator alarms inadvertently removes or alters the existing aggregate root alarm or reverts treat_missing_data, and no child AC catches the regression.
Epic completion verifier checks AC4 and finds no child acceptance criterion or test asserting the existing alarms persist / missing-data setting unchanged.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to S2 (the child that already edits monitoring_autodeploy.tf) an AC and test asserting the pre-existing root alarm and data alarm remain present with treat_missing_data unchanged, or add an explicit epic-level regression check covering all children that touch monitoring Terraform.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile S4's /var/tmp cap/reaper with 3e92's /var/tmp/rebar-evidence trap-cleaned evidence path so evidence capture is not truncated or prematurely reaped.
evidence: S4 What/AC: '/var/tmp has documented age cleanup and an actual enforced size ceiling on the Gerrit host' plus 'byte cap with a quota-capable mount/path or a bounded host cleanup service/timer'.

3e92 comment (disposition): 'the runbook documents /var/tmp/rebar-evidence/<ticket>-<stamp>/ with a trap-based delete bound AT SPAWN, which self-cleans on process exit irrespective of what /var/tmp is' - evidence dumps were ~5.2G each.
Parent AC5 requires 3e92 to be 'resolved or explicitly dispositioned before epic close', and parent Context item 3 folds 3e92 in, making it an in-scope sibling for consistency.
findings.finding: Conflicting assumption between S4's /var/tmp size cap and the carried-over sibling scowlful-bovine-dragonfly (3e92), which documents /var/tmp/rebar-evidence as the trap-cleaned evidence/scratch location.
scenarios: S4 installs a /var/tmp byte cap/quota; a live investigation writing ~5.2G evidence dumps under /var/tmp/rebar-evidence hits the cap or is reaped by S4's bounded cleanup timer before the trap fires, corrupting or truncating in-flight evidence.
S4's age-cleanup timer deletes /var/tmp/rebar-evidence directories before the spawning process's trap-based cleanup runs, defeating 3e92's documented mechanism.
findings.suggested_fix: In S4 scope, note the /var/tmp/rebar-evidence evidence path from 3e92 and either size the cap to accommodate documented evidence bounds or exclude the trap-managed evidence subtree from the cleanup timer's reaping, and cross-link 3e92.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the overlay2 accounting/prune boundary between S2 (image/build-cache layers) and S5 (writable/exited-container layers) so metrics do not double-count and prune/reaper actions do not conflict.
evidence: S2 What: 'Configure Docker/BuildKit-supported GC ceilings for Docker image/overlay2 accumulation' and 'never direct deletion under /var/lib/docker'; S2 grounding cites overlay2 image/container layers under /var/lib/docker/overlay2.

S5 What: 'Bound writable container layer growth ... otherwise install a bounded periodic reaper for exited containers'; S5 grounding cites writable container layers as the upperdir/diff under /var/lib/docker/overlay2.

Both children add observability metrics and CloudWatch alarms keyed to overlay2/Docker footprint (S2: 'Docker overlay/image ... usage/cap'; S5: 'writable/exited-container layer usage/cap'), and both integrate prune/reaper behavior against the same Docker storage tree.
findings.finding: Scope overlap / implicit shared state between S2 and S5 over Docker overlay2 accounting and prune behavior.
scenarios: S2's Docker image/layer usage metric and S5's writable-container-layer metric both parse /var/lib/docker/overlay2 sizes and either double-count the same bytes or disagree on attribution, so the two per-generator alarms fire on overlapping data.
S2's GC/prune policy and S5's exited-container reaper both act on overlay2 diffs; running them independently can race or one can undo the other's accounting assumptions.
findings.suggested_fix: In S2 and S5 grounding/scope, explicitly partition overlay2: S2 measures/caps image+build-cache layers only; S5 measures/caps writable (upperdir) + exited-container layers only, and name the shared observability.sh parsing seam so the two metrics are disjoint.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a baseline-measurement/spike step (observe steady-state and peak consumption per accumulator: Docker layers+cache, /var/tmp, journald, gate scratch) whose data derives the cap and alarm-threshold values in the child implementation/ADR.
evidence: Plan asserts native-GC caps ('SystemMaxUse', 'maxUsedSpace' / '--keep-storage') without stating how the numeric ceilings are sized
'The root volume was grown 30->60 GiB ... that is headroom only, not the fix: an unbounded generator can fill 60 GiB as readily as 30 GiB' — argues sizing matters but gives no derivation method
Scaffold-only scope defers values to children, but no measurement/baseline step is named to feed cap selection
findings.finding: The bounded-ceiling architecture rests on per-accumulator cap values (Docker maxUsedSpace/--keep-storage, journald SystemMaxUse, /var/tmp quota, gate-scratch EBS size) and per-generator alarm thresholds, but the epic names no step to derive these caps from measured baseline consumption — they risk being asserted rather than data-driven, which is the exact failure mode (a cap that self-fills) the epic exists to prevent.
findings.location: Operator-approved design items 1-2; AC 'Each named root accumulator has an enforced cap and its own CloudWatch alarm at/near cap.'
scenarios: A guessed Docker build-cache cap set too high still lets a burst fill root before its alarm fires; set too low and it thrashes GC and slows builds
findings.suggested_fix: In S0 (or a dedicated measurement child) require a short measurement window that records per-consumer high-water usage on the 60 GiB host, and size each cap and its at-cap alarm from that data rather than asserting round numbers.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile Scope ('no ADR file is created by this scaffold-only work') with AC1 ('ADR 0110 finalized and landed') — state explicitly whether ADR landing belongs to this epic or is delegated to child S0.
evidence: Scope: 'This epic scaffolds and later implements the approved architecture only... no ADR file is created by this scaffold-only work.'
AC1: 'ADR 0110 is finalized and landed in docs/adr/ with number marker and index update if required by repo convention.'
findings.finding: The Scope section says 'no ADR file is created by this scaffold-only work' while Acceptance Criterion 1 requires 'ADR 0110 is finalized and landed in docs/adr/... with number marker and index update'. These two statements point the implementer in opposite directions on whether an ADR file is produced within this epic's boundary.
findings.location: Scope section vs Acceptance Criteria line 1
scenarios: An implementer working the scaffold reads Scope and does not create the ADR file; a reviewer checking AC1 marks it unmet.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify that AC1 is satisfied by child S0 landing the ADR, and adjust Scope to say the scaffold epic does not itself write the ADR but tracks its landing via S0.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the default mechanism (or the decision criterion) for the /var/tmp cap and for writable-container-layer capping, so the executor need not re-decide, keeping the 'hard cap + dedicated alarm' constraint enforceable in either branch.
evidence: 'tmpfiles cleanup plus a real size/quota mechanism where required'
'runtime storage quota where supportable, or bounded periodic reaping of exited containers'
findings.finding: Scope bullet 1 leaves two real design choices unresolved in the plan text: '/var/tmp (tmpfiles cleanup plus a real size/quota mechanism where required)' and writable-layer capping via 'runtime storage quota where supportable, or bounded periodic reaping of exited containers'. Both defer a mechanism selection to the executor without stating the default or the deciding criterion.
scenarios: An implementer sizing the /var/tmp cap does not know whether a quota is 'required' or which of the two writable-layer approaches to adopt.
findings.suggested_fix: In S0/ADR, name the concrete mechanism per consumer (e.g. XFS project quota vs periodic reap) or state 'default to bounded periodic reaping unless runtime storage quota is supportable on the host kernel'.
